    Temporal beta diversity: losses and gains at each site

    Source: R/beta-uniqueness.R
    beta_tbi.Rd

    Compares the composition of each site at two times with the temporal beta diversity index (TBI) of Legendre (2019). The dissimilarity of each site between the two surveys is split into species losses (b) and gains (c), and a permutation test identifies the sites whose change is exceptional. With the percentage difference (Bray-Curtis) the losses and gains are in abundance; with Sorensen and Jaccard they are in species. The results match adespatial::TBI().

    Usage

    beta_tbi(
  data,
  time,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  index = c("bray", "sorensen", "jaccard"),
  nperm = 999,
  .by = NULL
)

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

    time

    <tidy-select> The column with the survey time. It must have exactly two values within each group; the earlier (in sort order or factor level) is the first survey.

    site, species

    <tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

    abundance

    <tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

    index

    "bray" (percentage difference, default), "sorensen" or "jaccard".

    nperm

    Number of permutations for the test of each site. Each species is permuted independently among sites at both times. Use 0 to skip the test.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

    Value

    A td_tbi tibble with the grouping columns, the site column, losses and gains (B/den and C/den of Legendre 2019, which sum to tbi), tbi, change ("loss", "gain" or "none", whichever is larger), p_value and p_adjusted (Holm).

    References

    Legendre, P. (2019). A temporal beta-diversity index to identify sites that have changed in exceptional ways in space-time surveys. Ecology and Evolution, 9, 3500-3514. doi:10.1002/ece3.4984

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
surveys <- subset(portal_rodents, year %in% c(2016, 2019))
beta_tbi(surveys, time = year, site = plot, nperm = 99)
#> # A tibble: 24 × 7
#>     plot losses  gains   tbi change p_value p_adjusted
#>    <int>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <chr>    <dbl>      <dbl>

#>  2     2 0.113  0.0397 0.152 loss      0.94       1   
#>  3     3 0.442  0.0442 0.487 loss      0.39       1   
#>  4     4 0.258  0.0710 0.329 loss      0.7        1   
#>  5     5 0.395  0      0.395 loss      0.49       1   
#>  6     6 0.225  0.0490 0.275 loss      0.78       1   
#>  7     7 0.228  0.0652 0.293 loss      0.75       1   
#>  8     8 0.0859 0.117  0.203 gain      0.92       1
